name: Handle field
summary: Finds an Atmosphere account by its handle or the person's name. It forgives how people type handles, suggests accounts as they type, and says when it understood something differently.

when: To find someone's Atmosphere account in Front Door, or to type the handle from a recovery email.

whenNot.text: To choose a new handle when signing up.

anatomy.description: Matching accounts, as a list under the input. “Did you mean” suggestions are in the automated style.
An error, or what the field understood, such as “We read sam@bsky.social as @sam.bsky.social”.

props.name: label
props.description: The field's label. Pass a catalogue string.

props.name: hint
props.description: Help under the label, such as an example. Pass a catalogue string.

props.name: error
props.description: The error message. Setting it marks the field invalid; clearing it marks it valid. The app validates.

props.name: name
props.description: The name the form submits the value under.

props.name: required
props.description: Whether it must be filled in. Screen readers say so; the app checks it.

props.name: suggestions
props.description: The accounts to suggest. The app looks them up when it hears doras-query.
props.items: handle, and optionally name, hostedBy, and didYouMean for a correction

states.name: Focus
states.description: A 2px focus ring, and a darker border.

states.name: Invalid
states.description: A red border and surface, and the error message under it.

states.name: Autofilled
states.description: Filled by the browser, in the theme's colours.

states.name: Suggesting
states.description: Matching accounts show under the input.

states.name: Did you mean
states.description: A suggestion that corrects a slip, in the automated style.

states.name: Understood differently
states.description: After leaving the field, an automated message says how it read what was typed.

events.name: doras-input
events.when: The value changes, but never while text is still being composed with an input method, such as Japanese. Once a field has an error, validate live on this.

events.name: change
events.when: Someone leaves the field after changing it.

events.name: doras-query
events.when: The text changes, so the app can look up accounts. Never while text is being composed.

accessibility.role: combobox, with a listbox of suggestions (ARIA 1.2)
accessibility.name: Its label.

keyboard.action: Chooses the highlighted suggestion, or submits the form.

screenReader: Announced as a combobox with its label, hint and any message.
The highlighted suggestion is announced as people move, and the number of matching accounts as suggestions appear.
announcements: “3 matching accounts”, politely, as suggestions change.
What it understood, politely, after someone leaves the field.
notes: It accepts a leading @, email-style handles such as sam@bsky.social, profile links, and common slips such as bsky.app.
Handles up to 253 characters break safely in the suggestions.
Lookups are the app's job: the field never calls the network.

guidelines: Labels are short nouns, such as “Email address”.
Hints give an example, not instructions.
Error messages say what to do: “Enter your email address”, not “Invalid input”.
The hint gives real examples, such as “It's on your profile, like sam.bsky.social”.

terms.meaning: An Atmosphere account's username, such as @sam.bsky.social. Always shown with an @ in running text.

dosAndDonts.do: Accept what people type and say how it was read.
dosAndDonts.dont: Reject a handle because it starts with @ or uses the wrong ending.

evidence.point: Errors tied to the field with aria-describedby, and an “Error:” prefix, so screen reader users hear what's wrong and where.
Validating on submit, then live, is the least stressful timing (decision in #1).
The combobox pattern with a listbox popup.
The prototype's research found people type handles as emails and use bsky.app for bsky.social; forgiving both avoids dead ends.
